O.content: The blue marker aligned with 'Service Quality' is higher on the page than every other blue marker.
The vertical axis is literally labeled 'Value' and has ticks increasing upward from 0 to 65.

B.text: If the vertical marker position on the 'Value' axis is the intended encoding of feedback share, a marker higher on that common axis represents a larger share; the task routes the highest such category to priority follow-up.
B.conditions: This conflicts with treating the printed percentages as the share values; the axis is labeled only 'Value,' so this interpretation is uncertain.

O.content: The title literally reads 'Public Service Feedback Share by Category'.
A '41%' inscription appears directly above the blue marker aligned with the 'Service Quality' x-axis label.
A '46%' inscription appears directly above the blue marker aligned with the 'Service Cost' x-axis label.
A '51%' inscription appears directly above the blue marker aligned with the 'Service Design' x-axis label.
A '42%' inscription appears directly above the blue marker aligned with the 'Support Access' x-axis label.
A '36%' inscription appears directly above the blue marker aligned with the 'Service Delivery' x-axis label.
A '10%' inscription appears directly above the blue marker aligned with the 'Other' x-axis label.

B.text: If the chart title identifies the displayed measure as public-service feedback share and each percent inscription is attached to its category's marker, the category with the largest printed percentage is the highest-share feedback category; the task routes that category to priority follow-up.
B.conditions: Assumes the percent inscriptions, rather than the vertically plotted marker positions on the generic 'Value' axis, encode feedback share.
